The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Core Economic Policy
Labour proposes fiscal rules requiring the current budget to balance and debt to fall as a share of GDP by the fifth forecast year. They commit to capping corporation tax at 25%, maintaining the triple lock on state pensions, and not increasing income tax, National Insurance, or VAT. They plan to abolish non-dom status, close private equity tax loopholes, and strengthen HMRC to tackle tax avoidance.

## Economic Growth Strategy
A National Wealth Fund (£7.3 billion) will invest in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, and green hydrogen. A new Industrial Strategy Council will guide long-term economic planning. Planning reform aims to build 1.5 million homes, with brownfield sites prioritised and strategic greenbelt release. Business rates will be reformed to support high streets against online retailers.

## Energy and Environment
Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland (£8.3 billion capitalisation), will partner with industry on clean power. Targets include doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind by 2030. The windfall tax on oil and gas companies will be extended and increased. No new oil/gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing fields continue operating. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion for home energy upgrades.

## NHS and Social Care
Plans include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling CT/MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and delivering the NHS workforce plan. Dentistry measures include 700,000 urgent appointments. Social care reform aims toward a National Care Service with national standards. Mental health legislation will be modernised.

## Education
Recruitment of 6,500 teachers funded by ending VAT exemption for private schools. Free breakfast clubs in all primary schools. 3,000 new primary school nurseries. Curriculum and assessment review planned. Skills England will coordinate training, with the Apprenticeships Levy reformed into a Growth and Skills Levy.

## Crime and Justice
A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee will recruit thousands of officers. Knife crime reduction targets halving within a decade, with new Young Futures hubs. Violence against women measures include specialist rape units in every police force and fast-tracked rape cases. Prisons will be expanded using planning powers.

## Immigration and Borders
A Border Security Command with counter-terrorism powers will target smuggling gangs. The Rwanda scheme will be scrapped. A returns unit with 1,000 additional staff will fast-track removals. Work visa policy will link to skills training requirements.

## Workers' Rights
Legislation within 100 days will ban exploitative zero-hours contracts, end fire-and-rehire practices, and establish day-one employment rights. A Single Enforcement Body will oversee compliance. The minimum wage will account for cost of living, with age bands removed.

## Constitutional Reform
Hereditary peers will lose voting rights. A mandatory retirement age of 80 will apply to Lords members. An Ethics and Integrity Commission will be established. Voting age will be lowered to 16.

## Devolution
A Council of Nations and Regions will bring together UK and devolved leaders. Structural fund allocation returns to devolved governments. Adult skills funding will be devolved to Combined Authorities.

## Foreign Policy
NATO commitment remains absolute, with a Strategic Defence Review within the first year. Support for Ukraine continues. An improved EU relationship is sought without rejoining the single market or customs union, including veterinary agreements and security cooperation. Palestinian statehood recognition is supported.

# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economy and Business
The manifesto proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation, creating apprenticeships and Lifelong Skills Grants, reforming business rates, and managing public finances responsibly. Plans include fixing UK-EU trade relations, replacing the apprenticeship levy with a broader skills levy, and expanding the British Business Bank. Tax proposals include reversing bank tax cuts, increasing Digital Services Tax to 6%, and reforming capital gains tax.

## Health and Care
The party commits to guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) through recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. Proposals include NHS dental access guarantees, mental health hubs for young people, a 62-day cancer treatment target, and free personal care based on Scotland's model. A new Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour increase) and cross-party commission on social care funding are proposed.

## Education
Plans include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing school funding above inflation, introducing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants. Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education are proposed, alongside free school meal expansion for children in poverty.

## Housing
The manifesto targets 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through garden cities and brownfield development. Renters would receive protection through banned no-fault evictions and three-year default tenancies. Proposals include abolishing residential leasehold and ending rough sleeping within the Parliament.

## Environment
Environmental plans include a sewage tax on water company profits, legally binding targets to "double nature" by 2050, planting 60 million trees annually, and a Clean Air Act. The party aims for net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030.

## Transport
Proposals include expanding EV charging infrastructure, reinstating plug-in car grants, freezing rail fares, extending rail electrification, and boosting bus services with local authority franchising powers. Road maintenance funding would shift to local councils for pothole repairs.

## Immigration and Asylum
The manifesto proposes scrapping the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme, processing asylum claims within three months, and allowing asylum seekers to work after three months. Work visa policy would transfer from the Home Office, and Youth Mobility Scheme expansion with the EU is proposed.

## Political Reform
Proposals include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, enshrining the Ministerial Code in law, reforming the House of Lords, capping political donations, and scrapping voter ID requirements.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP, with Army cuts reversed. The party supports NATO, maintaining nuclear deterrence, and Ukraine. European relations would follow a four-stage roadmap toward closer cooperation, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership. International development spending would return to 0.7% of national income.
